question: Which grid-storage battery scenario is unfolding by 2030?

scenarios.label: Lithium Lock-in
scenarios.description: LFP lithium-ion keeps >= 85% of new grid-storage GWh through 2030

scenarios.label: Sodium Surge
scenarios.description: sodium-ion takes >= 25% of new stationary-storage GWh by 2030

scenarios.label: Long-Duration Leap
scenarios.description: non-lithium 8-hour-plus technologies take >= 25% of new grid-storage capacity by 2030

indicators.text: Sodium-ion cells quoted at or below $50/kWh at GWh volume by at least two suppliers
indicators.source: supplier price sheets; battery price surveys

indicators.text: At least 30% of MW awarded in US/EU/China utility storage tenders in a year specifies 8-hour-plus duration
indicators.source: public tender awards (DOE, EU TSOs, NEA)

indicators.text: Lithium carbonate spot price stays below $15/kg for four consecutive quarters
Global grid-storage installations exceed 100 GWh in a calendar year
A top-5 cell maker commissions a sodium-ion line of 10 GWh/yr or more dedicated to stationary storage
A major market adopts capacity-market rules that pay duration-weighted credit beyond 4 hours
An iron-air or flow-battery project of 100 MW or more reaches commercial operation with published round-trip efficiency and availability
indicators.threshold: >= 100 MW in operation with published data

indicators.text: Government storage subsidies and mandates continue in the major markets
At least two announced sodium-ion gigafactories are cancelled or delayed by more than 12 months
Sodium-ion exceeds 10% of new stationary-storage GWh in China in a calendar year (industry-association data)
At least two long-duration projects above 100 MW are cancelled or re-scoped to 4-hour lithium
More than 3 GW of 8-hour-plus storage holds signed offtake contracts in a single market's interconnection queue
indicators.threshold: > 3 GW at >= 8 h with signed offtake
